newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold remains vulnerable to the downside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold remains vulnerable to the downside.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Monday's physical buying and short-covering has helped to turn the tide of downside pressure on gold, though several traders and analysts believe after a period of stability prices will resume their downside move.
Silver following a period of base building could head higher, while platinum is expected to hold recent ranges, they added.

GOLD - The snap away from a low of around $336.60 an ounce on Monday has helped to bolster near-term upside sentiment, though several traders and chartists are expecting downside pressure to emerge if prices fail to breach a downtrend line currently around $342.50.

"The buying on Monday was largely short-covering reacting to an oversold condition," one trader said. "Although it helped to drag gold away from its lows it did little to help the market's long term outlook which I believe is still down," the trader added.

Analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston said gold had to break above $342.50 to offset downside pressure. "If gold fails to break this level then we would more than likely see a further downside retracement," Jones said.
In early European trading gold was finding resistance around $340.00. At 0740 spot material was indicated at $339.15/$339.65 an ounce, against Monday's London close of $338.65/$339.15.
SILVER - Seen probing higher after recently building a base around $4.80.
Needs to break $4.96 to spark a move to $5.20/$5.25, Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston said.
Jones expected stiff support on moves to $4.60.
At 0745 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.82/4.84, versus $4.80/$4.82.
PLATINUM - Seen supported from a six-week uptrend line, though a break below levels between $400.00 and $402.00 could see a move to $385.00/$383.50.
Market needs to break above $440.00 to spark fresh strong upside momentum.
At 0745 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $415.00/420.00, against $418.50/$423.50.
